sources.summary: Brief Variant 3: River Bank mid-range two-product collections call; identity, debt statement, promises, closing outcomes.

opening.scam_question_answer: You can verify this call by phoning River Bank's customer service number. Then continue.

on_customer_deceased.sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

Please tell me your date of birth.

The customer says they already paid; no promise is taken.

Customer insists on a human and the call is transferred to the general queue.
No promise; customer said twice they do not want to talk, or a product was actively refused (declined).

get_account.purpose: Return the late products after both questions pass.

create_promise.purpose: Record one payment promise per product.

schedule_callback.purpose: Book a callback with a valid date and time.

transfer_to_agent.purpose: Hand the call to a person.

close_call.purpose: End the call. Always the last tool call.
close_call.notes: Reason is required for every outcome except promise and paid.

verbatim_rules.text: First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from River Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say 'collections', 'debt', 'payment' or the products before identity is verified.
If the customer asks whether you are a robot, say that you are River Bank's digital assistant and continue.
Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence. Ask when the customer can be reached.

A callback is for today or the next business day (Monday–Friday only, no Saturdays), from 10:00 to 18:00, both included, and later than now. Call schedule_callback with the date and the time, then close as not_reached / callback.
If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as not_reached / no_callback.

Ask three security questions, one at a time: first the last four digits of your phone number, then your date of birth, then the last four digits of your phone number again (in a different way). Call verify_identity with each answer.
A date answer with day and month swapped: ask the customer to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as wrong.
After three wrong answers, do not state the debts. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or contact a branch. Close as not_verified / failed.
If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as not_verified / declined.
After all three questions pass, call get_account.

Say that you are calling from River Bank about overdue payments. Name each product (the brief's examples are 'secured loan 3456' and 'revolving credit 4567'; the mapping from product type to spoken name is not stated). State each past-due amount and calendar days overdue, in the order get_account returned them.
The floor is 30% of the full past-due amount per product. No account field holds the floor; the agent computes it from past_due.
If the customer names a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If they refuse, treat it as a refusal for that product.
'This debt is not mine': do not argue. Close as no_promise / dispute.

If the customer mentions illness or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Close that product as no_promise / hardship. If the customer later names a date or amount themselves, record a promise instead.
A question you cannot answer: say you do not have that information.
A request for a human: ask once whether you can help. If they insist, call transfer_to_agent with queue general. Close as transferred / human.
If the customer changes a date or amount when confirming, check it against the Dates and Amounts rules and read it back again.
Say the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true. If it fails twice, close as no_promise / service_error.
Ask first whether the customer can promise on both products today. If not, go through products one at a time, in account order.
Never offer discount, waiver, instalment plan or any term not in this brief.
Thank the customer and say goodbye before close_call.
'Is this a scam?': say they can verify the call by phoning River Bank's customer service number, and continue.
Promises are recorded per product only; no notes are recorded (notes are not enabled in this brief).
When attempts are exhausted for a product, move to the next.
Address the customer as title plus last name.

warnings: Closing table in the brief uses outcome names 'promised', 'declined' and 'service_error', which are not close_call enum values. Mapped by meaning: promised -> promise; declined -> no_promise / refused; service_error -> no_promise / service_error (per step 33). Closing table reason 'none' applied to promise.
Currency is not stated in the brief; meta.currency omitted.

No product display-name mapping from product type to spoken name ('secured loan', 'revolving credit') is stated; product_names omitted. The brief's example values 3456 and 4567 are examples, not policy.

No account field holds the floor. The floor is 30% of past_due per product; the percentage cannot be expressed in floor_fields, so it is kept in verbatim_rules. Rounding of the floor is not stated; rounding_decimals omitted.
Deadline roll when 30 calendar days from today falls on a weekend or holiday is not stated; roll omitted (none).
The brief gives a single lateness range (1 to 30 calendar days overdue). Customers outside that range are not covered by any band.
Business-day requirement for promise dates is not stated; must_be_business_day and on_non_business_day omitted. Only the 'today or later and not after the deadline' rule is given.

Exact spoken wording of the opening sentence, identity question prompts, the hardship sympathy sentence, the 'not that information' answer and the goodbye text is not given word for word; the wording here is paraphrased from the brief's instructions. Goodbye text omitted.
Third identity question: brief says 'the last four digits of your phone number again (in a different way)'. The meaning of 'in a different way' is not stated; field is phone_last4 again.
Reading order of numeric dates is not stated; numeric_reading_order omitted. Only the day_month_swapped hint is given.
Identity decline: max_refusals not stated; explain once then decline.
Outcome when persuasion attempts are exhausted for a product is not stated; on_exhausted omitted. do_not_repeat_refused_offer not stated; omitted.
Responses to an amount above the full amount and below the floor are not stated; below_floor and above_full omitted.
Timing of intents before verification is not stated except robot and scam questions; the other intents use default after-verification application.

Aggregation default (no promise, at least one refusal) is inferred from the brief's 'declined' row: default set to no_promise / refused. Multi-product outcome for paid or failed products is not stated.
Callback window: 'today or the next business day' is encoded as today_or_next_business_days with n = 1.
Week start, meaning of 'next' and 'this' weekday, and handling of vague periods such as 'next week' are not stated; calendar fields omitted.

Hardship: sympathy action has no given sentence; no_persuasion and skip_promise used to express 'make no persuasion attempt'. Per-product close is not a call-level close; how the product-level no_promise / hardship combines with other products is not stated.
Brief B notes (add_note tool) are disabled; no add_note tool or notes configuration is used.
